reviewScope: Review only. This review does not mark DR-112 SATISFIED, does not qualify or demonstrate anything, does not authorize implementation, and does not apply or seal the candidate.
summary: The v5 authority, recovery, replay, and ownership repairs are materially present: recoveryAuthorityShape now contains application, reserved-threshold, and old-root/new-root/role-binding conjuncts; RECOVER-COMMIT references the full shape and separates DR-103 bytes from DR-112 envelope verification; the replay vector has a typed fail-closed disposition; and the v3 advisory plus both v4 verdicts are accurately recorded. Two non-fail-open contract defects prevent acceptance. First, the machine transition now has a bounded toFunction, but the normative ceremonyTermination schema still uses the undeclared token 'computed' while appliesFindingsOf says that finding is folded. Second, the new ENVELOPE-INACTIVE branches do not establish a unique audit reason: defaultTransition and the PRESENT/COMMIT fallbacks explicitly assign competing reasons to inactive cases, whenFailed is not restricted to ACTIVE failure, and TRUSTED EV-INSTALL still falls back to INSTALL-NOT-TRUSTED despite naming ACTIVE as a TRUSTED-entry prerequisite. At 0 blockers and 2 SHOULD-FIX findings, DR-112 remains OPEN and this verdict authorizes no implementation.

shouldFix.title: The abort repair leaves the undeclared 'computed' target in the joined termination schema
shouldFix.measurement: The EV-RECOVER-ABORT transition is repaired locally: to='same-or-named'; declaredMetaTarget matches; candidatesInOrder contains four declared states in safety order; else is ST-UNBOOTSTRAPPED; and never is ST-TRUSTED. However auditAndWaiver.ceremonyTermination is unchanged from v4 and still prescribes '{ role, from: ST-RECOVERY, to: computed, ... }'. Claude v4 S-1 explicitly measured that occurrence as part of the undeclared-target defect. v5 records CODEX-V3-A1 as folded, lists nothing in notFoldedThisSuccessor, and says the abort target is declared, while one of the two joined abort records still exposes the old undeclared token.
shouldFix.whyShouldFix: The transition function is safety-bounded, so this does not create a path to ST-TRUSTED and is not a blocker. It does leave two incompatible conformance surfaces for the same accepted abort: the event transition says toFunction result, while the termination-record schema says computed. An audit implementation or fixture cannot mechanically validate the joined to-state from the latter, and the successor finding ledger overstates repair completion.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Replace the ceremonyTermination to field with the actual named toFunction result, or a structured reference to that function whose codomain is the four candidates plus ST-UNBOOTSTRAPPED. Add that path to the successor roster and only then record CLAUDE-V4-S1 / CODEX-V4-S1 / CODEX-V3-A1 as fully folded.

shouldFix.title: INACTIVE TRUSTED-entry refusal does not have one deterministic reason
shouldFix.measurement: Transitions 0-2 now say whenInactive => ENVELOPE-INACTIVE, yet EV-PRESENT-PAYLOAD's fallback expressly includes a 'not-yet-active TRUSTED-entry payload' and assigns PAYLOAD-NOT-ADMISSIBLE. Transition 16 says whenInactive => ENVELOPE-INACTIVE, but its unqualified whenFailed branch assigns RECOVERY-COMMIT-REFUSED and the event fallback expressly includes 'TRUSTED-entry still INACTIVE' under that same reason. defaultTransition still says a named member with a false guard takes the event fallback and never defines whenInactive/whenFailed precedence. Independently, transition 3 calls ACTIVE a TRUSTED-entry prerequisite, targets ST-TRUSTED, has no whenInactive branch, and therefore assigns INSTALL-NOT-TRUSTED through its fallback when inactive. FC-ENVELOPE-INACTIVE nevertheless promises exactly ENVELOPE-INACTIVE for every path that would enter ST-TRUSTED.
shouldFix.whyShouldFix: Every competing branch refuses, so there is no fail-open behavior and this is not a blocker. The exact refusal identity is nevertheless part of the audit contract and negative-fixture oracle. The same inactive attempted event can be read as producing two different vocabulary members, and the INSTALL path produces a third; an implementation cannot satisfy the stated exact fixture without choosing an unstated precedence.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Define structured branch-selection semantics before defaultTransition, or split the inactive cases into explicit guarded members that win before fallback. Restrict whenFailed to ACTIVE-but-other-conjunct-failed, remove inactive cases from the PRESENT and COMMIT fallback notes, and give TRUSTED EV-INSTALL an ENVELOPE-INACTIVE branch if the exact fixture truly covers every ST-TRUSTED-targeting TRUSTED-entry path; otherwise narrow the fixture and invariant explicitly.
